result:
Read the ledger entry, the before/after, and the guide.

**Short version: it's tidying — but it's the same tidying twice, and that's the part worth carrying into the look session.**

What the numbers actually say. Eleven pixels, all erased, nothing added, nothing recolored. Every one of them sits in the bottom-center of the cell — y 14–15 of a 16px frame, under the hen's feet, shifting with the leg position through the walk. The Farmer edit forty seconds earlier is the identical shape: seventeen pixels, all erased, all at the base of the body. He isn't restating a silhouette. He's removing something opaque from the ground under a character, twice, and both times he wrote the same reason: *I want to see the background through it.*

Ignore the "silhouette moved" flag. The tool raises that whenever alpha changes, so any erase trips it. There's no evidence here of him redrawing a shape.

Does it contradict the guide? No — pure white isn't in any ramp, and the guide already says shadows are hue-shifted, never grey or black. He enforced a rule the guide implies but never writes down: **a sprite may not put opaque pixels on the ground beneath itself.** That's a real gap. The guide talks about ramps, outlines and saturation-pop; it says nothing about the ground-contact zone, which is exactly where a generated sprite's leftover backdrop always lands. One line for the look session, not an amendment now.

The thing that needs doing regardless of taste: **HQ's sprite editor only showed him a quarter of each sheet.** Chicken exposes cells 0–3, the right-facing walk — but that sheet carries its own left frames at 4–7 rather than mirroring, and he never saw them. Farmer exposes the facing-down row, 4 of 16. So both fixes are almost certainly half-applied: the hen stops occluding the background walking right and keeps doing it walking left. I couldn't confirm at the pixel level from here — I don't have the sandbox permission to inspect the sheet directly — but the layout notes make it near-certain.

Next steps: Yuki sweeps both full sheets for opaque near-white in the ground-contact zone, and Ravi checks whether the generation pipeline's alpha step is what leaves it — this should be fixed once at the pipeline, not hand-erased frame by frame. I'll bring the ground-contact rule to your look session as a candidate line rather than editing the unsigned guide.

<remember>Daniel's hand edits to sprites (Chicken, Farmer, 2026-09-03) are erase-only — no colors added or recolored — and both removed opaque near-white from the ground-contact zone under the character with the same stated reason: the background must show through beneath a sprite. Two data points toward a style-guide rule the draft doesn't have. Also: HQ's sprite editor exposes only one row/direction per entity (Chicken cells 0–3 of 0–7; Farmer the facing-down row of 16), so his fixes are structurally half-applied.</remember>

conversation.text:
> HQ's sprite editor only showed him a quarter of each sheet. 

Why aren't you also creating a story to fix this?

You're right — I flagged it and stopped there. That's the gap you've told me not to leave.

Checked it just now so the story is accurate: the editor doesn't read the sheet, it reads the preview frame list in HQ's entity catalog. Chicken's entry lists four rectangles; the sheet has eight, and its own note says cells 4–7 are the left-facing walk rather than a mirror. Farmer lists four of sixteen. So the editor is showing exactly what the catalog told it to show, and the catalog was written for a little looping preview, not for editing.

What I want filed, three pieces:

**Rin** — the sprite editor opens the whole sheet, every cell, with the preview frames just highlighted as "this is what animates." Editing a quarter of a sheet without being told so is the actual bug.

**Yuki** — fill in the full frame lists in the catalog and sweep both sheets for opaque near-white in the ground-contact zone, so your two fixes land on every frame instead of half.

**Ravi** — check whether the generation pipeline's alpha step is leaving that white behind. If it is, fix it there; nobody should be hand-erasing backdrop pixels.

The ground-contact rule still waits for your look session — that one's taste, not tidying.

<remember>Daniel expects a gap I notice to arrive as a filed story with an owner, not as an observation in prose — he pushed back on this directly (2026-09-03, sprite editor showing only preview frames). HQ's sprite editor edits the preview frame list in hq/data/entities.json, not the actual sheet, which is why entity edits are partial: Chicken lists 4 of 8 cells, Farmer 4 of 16.</remember>
